findings.claim: R4 mitigation for CG-R4-001 explicitly required a third test in test_signing_keys_outage.py that patches subprocess.run to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired and asserts degraded-envelope + cross-resource key_id=None. This test was not delivered in fr4; test_signing_keys_outage.py contains only the two pre-existing tests covering RuntimeError paths. The blast-radius fix is correct in production code but unguarded against regression.
findings.evidence: test_signing_keys_outage.py has 74 lines and exactly two test functions: test_snapshot_degrades_when_committed_signing_keys_are_malformed (duplicate current=true markers → RuntimeError 'multiple current signing keys declared') and test_snapshot_logs_and_degrades_for_empty_committed_signing_keyring (empty keyring → RuntimeError 'contains no ssh-ed25519 key entries'). Neither patches subprocess.run to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired. R4 mitigation stated: 'Add a third test in test_signing_keys_outage.py that patches subprocess.run to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired and asserts: (a) catalog.snapshot() does not raise; (b) read_static(scp://security/signing-keys)[error] is not None; (c) read_static(scp://decisions)[key_id] is None.' fr4 commit 3bc6fe6 applied only the except-clause change.
findings.impact: No regression protection for the TimeoutExpired blast-radius fix. A future refactor narrowing the except clause back to 'except RuntimeError' or 'except (RuntimeError, OSError)' without realising subprocess.TimeoutExpired is NOT an OSError subclass would silently reopen the MAJ blast-radius vector.
findings.mitigation: Add to test_signing_keys_outage.py: a test_snapshot_degrades_on_git_timeout function using monkeypatch (or unittest.mock.patch) to make subprocess.run raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(cmd=['git','show'], timeout=30) for the signing-keys call; assert catalog.snapshot() does not raise; assert read_static('scp://security/signing-keys')['error'] is not None; assert all STATIC_RESOURCE_URIS payloads have key_id=None; assert caplog contains 'degrading MCP resource snapshot: signing-keys unavailable'.

findings.claim: R4 MIN carry-forward (unresolved in fr4): propose() is already live in the 021D server before its 021E anti-spam rate-limit (10/caller/hour) and silent-rot banner are implemented. R4 mitigation required an explicit tracked-forward note in WP-SCP-021 §4 021E row naming the two unmet dimensions. No such note was added in fr4.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-021-scp-as-mcp-server.md §4 021E row (line 94) describes rate-limit and silent-rot banner as 021E deliverables — this is pre-existing plan text, unchanged. No new language explicitly flags that propose() is already registered in the live 021D server without these features and that 021E dispatch must verify them against the running implementation. fr4 commit 3bc6fe6 was limited to the resources.py except clause change; no plan amendment.
findings.impact: 021E dispatcher and reviewer have no governance checkpoint noting propose() is pre-deployed without rate-limit or banner; AC §9-5 ('rate-limit + normalised-hash anti-dup exercised; silent-rot banner appears in proposal body') can silently pass at 021E without explicitly verifying the already-live propose() implementation satisfies both dimensions.
findings.mitigation: Amend WP-SCP-021 §4 021E row with: 'NOTE (tracked-forward from 021D): propose() is already registered in the live server as of 021D; 021E must close: (a) time-window rate-limit counter ≤ 10/caller/hour in propose_impl; (b) silent-rot banner text auto-injected into proposal body markdown. Both must be tested.' No code change required in 021D.

findings.claim: Carry-forward now verified in R5: 'referencing' is imported directly in test_resource_schemas.py line 7 ('from referencing import Registry, Resource') but is absent from pyproject.toml. jsonschema is declared as a runtime dependency (pyproject.toml line 21: 'jsonschema>=4.25.0' in [project.dependencies]) when it is only used by test code.
findings.evidence: test_resource_schemas.py:7 'from referencing import Registry, Resource' — confirmed live. pyproject.toml grep returns only 'jsonschema>=4.25.0' on line 21 (runtime [project.dependencies]); 'referencing' does not appear. No dev optional-dependencies entry for either package.
findings.impact: CI environments using strict --no-deps installs or a minimal venv that excludes dev extras will fail to import referencing, producing ImportError that masks the real issue. Shipping jsonschema in runtime deps inflates the installed footprint for consumers who do not run the test suite.
findings.mitigation: Add 'referencing>=0.30' to [project.optional-dependencies] dev (or test) extras. Move jsonschema to the same dev/test optional-dependencies group if no production module imports it directly.
